chunks: Abu Ali Al-Ashary, from Muhammad ibn Abdul Jabbar, from Ibn Fazzal, from Ibrahim ibn Akhi Abi Shibl, from Abu Shibl, who said:

Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said to me, initiating the conversation: 'You loved us, and the people hated us; you believed us, and the people called us liars; you connected with us, and the people distanced themselves from us. So Allah made your life our life, and your death our death.'
By Allah, there is nothing between a man and the delight which Allah keeps for him except that his soul reaches this place,' and he gestured with his hand to his throat and extended the skin.

Then he repeated that, and by Allah, he was not satisfied until he swore to me, saying: 'By Allah, besides Whom there is no god, my father Muhammad ibn Ali (peace be upon him) narrated that to me. O Abu Shibl!'

Are you not pleased that you pray and they pray, so it is accepted from you and not from them? Are you not pleased that you give zakat and they give zakat, so it is accepted from you and not from them? Are you not pleased that you perform Hajj and they perform Hajj, so Allah, Exalted is His mention, accepts from you and does not accept from them?
By Allah, the prayer is not accepted except from you, nor the zakat except from you, nor the Hajj except from you.

So fear Allah, Exalted and Glorified is He, for you are in a truce (or period of ease), and fulfill the trusts. When the people are distinguished, at that time every group goes with its desire, but you go with the truth, as long as you obeyed us.
Are not the judges, the rulers, and the people of fatwa (jurists) among them?' I said, 'Yes.'

He (peace be upon him) said: 'So fear Allah, Exalted and Glorified is He, for you cannot tolerate all the people. The people have taken from here and there, but you have taken from where Allah, Exalted and Glorified is He, has taken.'

Indeed, Allah, Exalted and Glorified is He, chose Muhammad (peace be upon him and his family) from His servants, so you have chosen the choice of Allah. So fear Allah and fulfill the trusts to the black and the white, even if he is Haruri or if he is Shami.
ai.seo_question: Why are the prayers and zakat of the Shia accepted while those of others are not, according to this hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi underscores the Shia doctrine of 'Qabul al-A'mal' (acceptance of deeds) being contingent upon love for the Ahl al-Bayt, contrasting the spiritual validity of the faithful against the general public. Imam al-Sadiq (as) reinforces this by linking their election to Allah’s choice of the Prophet and his progeny, urging steadfastness in fulfilling trusts amidst the rise of diverse, often divergent, religious authorities. The narrative serves as a theological foundation for the Shia identity, emphasizing that true worship is inseparable from correct allegiance to the Imams.
